arc.name: the claim
arc.why: Not the wreck — twelve frames of one video survived. The day makes an assertion and then, seventeen years later, supplies its own evidence. It also qualifies as the claim over the ladder because two of its four posts are 2008 and the fourth is 2009: too shallow to walk through time.

register.name: D · Duotone
register.why: Pictures and their absence carry it. One image dead, one video's twelve frames alive, one post with no media at all. Halftoning the survivors into the ink and leaving the dead as broken boxes is the day's whole subject rendered as a colour state.

hook.what: The EDIT sentence at the size of the frame, over the twelve surviving frames halftoned in the ink
hook.why: It is the strongest thing the day has by a distance: Iain in 2009 watching a video die overnight, keeping the corpse deliberately as evidence, and asking how long the others have. This project is the answer to that question. It survives the square crop because it is one sentence and a texture.

line.text: I wonder how long the others will last?

caption: 9 September 2009. Iain notices one of the videos he posted the night before has already been taken down, and leaves the broken embed in on purpose — "an artifact of 'the man' exercising his right to shut stuff down. I wonder how long the others will last?" Seventeen years on, one of them is still up and we pulled twelve frames off it. The day's other three posts are from 2008: Gordon Ramsay becoming a video game, a music widget with a 'needle drop' function, and seventy-five characters about laughing out loud in an office. Link in bio for the originals.

openQuestions: Slide 5 is one sentence alone on a slide. Deliberate, but it is the riskiest slide here and the easiest to cut to six.

The turntable and vinyl stickers reach this day via the word 'track' in the DJdownload post, having been fetched for 11-26. Legitimate under the rule, but it is the first case of the library crossing days — worth watching.
